name: tcw
description: Taxonomy · Capabilities · Work — a storage-abstracted framework for describing and evolving a software project.

interface.shortDescription: Skills for the tcw workflow: taxonomy, capabilities, work tracking, and documentation sync.
interface.longDescription: tcw (Taxonomy · Capabilities · Work) is a storage-abstracted framework for describing and evolving a software project along three axes. This plugin ships seventeen skills — the three axis drivers `taxonomy`, `capabilities`, and `work`; five command skills for the everyday workflow, `commands-plan-work`, `commands-drive-work-to-completion`, `commands-verify-work`, `commands-process-inbox`, and `commands-pause-work`, which stops the work in hand, writes down what resuming needs and waits for you; `configure` for changing a project's TCW configuration; `setup` for setting TCW up and repairing the CLI; `work-stage`, which hands you any lifecycle stage's working document and the instructions your project resolves for it as one read; `work-create`, which turns an idea into a work item after checking what the board and the work inbox already track; `extras-report` for filing bugs and suggestions upstream; `extras-triage-issues` for turning your own project's GitHub issues into tracked work; `post-mortem` for finding which lifecycle stage could first have caught a problem; `extras-autonomous-work` for driving items to completion unattended; and `documentation-sync`, a cross-cutting process skill that keeps docs in step with code — driving the tcw workflow from inside an AI coding agent.
interface.defaultPrompt: Help me use tcw to plan and track work.
